steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Mmph... mmph!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Mmph—!

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Give it up already, will you?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Don't blame me for handing you over to the Inquisition. We all have to look out for ourselves.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: I'll take the cloth out of your mouths if you'll quiet down.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: (Nods hesitantly)

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: I'll be quiet...

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Yeah, if you know what's good for you.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: But even if you hand us and the compass over, that doesn't mean things will end well for you. Ever thought about that?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Yeah...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: The bodies of your dead crewmates are still decorating the flagpole outside of town. You sure you won't end up joining them?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: No... Not here either...

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Where is that blasted compass? The chaval puts it back here every night!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Is this what you're looking for, Javi?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You shouldn't have come back so soon, Juana.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: On the contrary, I think I returned at precisely the right time.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Señora, I... I don't have a choice.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Put down the knife, Javi. I taught you how to use it. You don't stand a chance.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You're injured. Might not even be hard.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: How did it come to this?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: What dissatisfaction could possibly have driven you to point your blade at me?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I was never unhappy with you. I supported every decision you ever made, every idea you ever had.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: When my mother left me, you took my hand and said we were family.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Ever since then, I've never been unhappy with you.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Then why?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: It's for your good, Juana... for you...

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Lies. I'm standing right here.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Tell me! How is it my for own good when you're pointing a blade at me?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: The Juana I know wouldn't put the entire fleet in danger for her own selfish desires. She's a brave, wise leader we can trust.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You're not her. You're just a...

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Spit it out!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Just a pathetic woman who refuses to face reality, drowning herself in the passions of the past!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: I've told you time and again...

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: The ocean is not our past. It's our future.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: That's what you want to believe. No one else in the fleet does. The old generation is dead. The stories they told should've died with them.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Give me the compass, Juana. Don't make me take it.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: I'd like to see you try.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Don't you understand?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You really think I made the decision to hand it over to the Inquisition on my own?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: A mutiny... So this is what was waiting for me.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: What a surprise.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: All I want is the compass. All they want is a peaceful future.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Give us what we want, and you can still be our leader. Nothing has to change.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Nothing will change? Don't tell me you actually believe that, Javi?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Stop fooling yourself. At the very least, I wouldn't trust you like before.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You're right.

steps.name: Hesitant Sailor
steps.text: Sorry to do this to you, boss, but the sea's no place to call home.

steps.name: Hesitant Sailor
steps.text: We just wanna leave the Flat and live a better life.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Put down your weapons, go back to your tents, and I'll pretend none of this happened.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: We're out of options, mates.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: We can't keep fooling ourselves.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: ...Sorry I'm late.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Mmph—! Let go of me!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: The hell I will, you finshit eater. I still got the marks from the ropes!

steps.name: Hesitant Sailor
steps.text: You said nobody would know about this mutiny, Javier!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: ...Mierda!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I found Señor Rus 'lost' on the Salt Flat, so I brought him back.

steps.name: Hesitant Sailor
steps.text: What's this about, Javier?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Now now, I wouldn't make any wrong moves if I were you. Not if you still care about your friend here.

steps.name: Hesitant Sailor
steps.text: Shut up! This is none of your business, outsider!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: What do you suggest we do then?

steps.name: Angry Sailor
steps.text: To fight them of course! Burn that blasted town to the ground and take back what's ours!

steps.name: Angry Sailor
steps.text: You're going against the boss over some finshit scheme to kneel before the Inquisition? Did you lose your spine like a gutted fin?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: They just killed so many of us and took our supplies, and you can't wait to grovel to them, Javier?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: I know Juana taught you better than that.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: We're tired, wounded, and can barely muster up half a scrap of food. How're we supposed to fight?

steps.name: Hesitant Sailor
steps.text: Besides, those Inquisition capullos wouldn't even be after us if that dumb girl didn't bring the compass here.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Er, Señora Juana...?

steps.name: Angry Sailor
steps.text: So just give them the girl! What do you think you're doing, turning yourselves in along with her?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Teach...?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Enough, this isn't helping.

steps.name: Hesitant Sailor
steps.text: Yeah, why haven't we handed her over yet?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Urk!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Señores and señoras, if I may say something...

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You shut your mouth!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Uh...
Cold sweat runs down Pascuala's back as the pirates point their cutlasses at her.
She gulps and tries to wipe her sweaty palms on her pants.
She knows there is only ever one way to get what she wants: fight for it with her own two hands.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Come on, guys, what are you doing to one little girl?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Pelirrojito, you—

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: So many adults in the room, and the best you can come up with is to hand over a child?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Enough already!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Hey, I'm speaking up for you!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: I know! But I can speak for myself!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: You folks wanna hand me over? Sure! Why not?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: I get why you'd want to beat the finshit out of me, and I'm sure you get why I scammed you.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Violence and deception. That's how we survive. That's all we know.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: But you know how they do things in town. Do you really think handing me and the compass over will help you even one bit?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: But if you don't, the Inquisition bastards will keep hunting you, and that won't go so well for you either, no?

steps.name: Angry Sailor
steps.text: So what's your point? We're screwed either way?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: One week.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Give us one week to fix up that compass!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Yes. I just need a little more time.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: If he succeeds, the compass will guide us to the sea, where those finshits will never find us again!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: If he doesn't, well, it won't be too late to hand me over and see how that goes!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Not like we could escape with the whole crew watching our every move. What difference could one week make?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: In Iberia, you escape one barren hellhole only to end up in another.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Outside the country, your life isn't your own without cold hard cash! It belongs to whoever's paying you!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Señora Juana isn't taking you out to sea just to die. What do you think she's trying to do?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: You should know better than me how smart she is. She'd have been way better off leaving your sorry asses behind ages ago.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: She could've held your lives in her hands and made you work for pennies, but she didn't.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: She just wanted you to be free.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: That compass is your ticket to fame and fortune, just like your forefathers! How could you call yourselves pirates, when you've never even seen the sea?
Pascuala feels like her heart is about to leap from her chest. Her clothes are soaked with sweat.
The room is completely silent. She forces a smile and turns to look at Juana, Teach, Isidro, and Elysium behind her, who answer with approving eyes.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Uh... still letting all that sink in?

steps.name: Hesitant Sailor
steps.text: I got no problem waiting a week. But someone'll be watching you the whole time.

steps.name: Angry Sailor
steps.text: Fine by us.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Anyone else?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I object.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I said, I object!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You're letting a teenage girl make a fool of you like this? You think she knows the first thing about compasses or sailing?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I promise you, if we just get that compass and give it to the Inquisition, then—

steps.name: Hesitant Sailor
steps.text: Sorry, Javier...
One sailor puts down his weapon, then another, then another. One by one, they walk out of the captain's quarters.
Only Javier and Juana are left, facing off.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: I have a mission for you and Rus, Javier. You are not to return to the fleet until it's completed.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Go and pack up. You leave at nightfall.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: (Whisper) Let's go, Javier...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: How's it going?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: We've almost reached the deadline...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: If, and I mean, IF we fail...

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: How about you just don't fail!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Señora Juana gave you her full support. Think of everything she's done for this.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Exiling Javier and Rus, two of her most trusted crewmates...

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: She... she even killed her own...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: That's enough, Pascuala.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: He knows what needs to be done.

steps.name: Anxious Sailor
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Impassionate Sailor
steps.text: Stop sighing your heart out.

steps.name: Anxious Sailor
steps.text: Today's the day. Aren't you anxious?

steps.name: Impassionate Sailor
steps.text: What's the use of worrying? Just think about what life would be like if that compass really paid off.

steps.name: Anxious Sailor
steps.text: Aye... but what if he fails?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Man, they're really packed around the room. Not even a grain of salt could slip through.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: I have a bad feeling about this...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: C'mon, don't jinx us like that.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Still...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: He's refused any help these last few days, holing himself up in his lab...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: He wouldn't let us participate, not even today. Said the experiments require precise control, said that he didn't want to be disturbed.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: But if I know anything about him, and I definitely do... he's doing this because he doesn't want to drag anyone else into it.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Maybe he's preparing to fail.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: But the repairs aren't done yet, are they?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: That's just how Thorns is. He always expects the worst, and braces himself for it.

steps.name: Anxious Sailor
steps.text: What was that?!
The layers of Arts energy field on the transmutation table collapse in an instant. The metallic substance that had gleamed with a shiny glow a moment ago is now a pile of charred mud.
Isidro pulled the probe back just in time to avoid damaging it, but the compass parts he had assembled now lie in pieces.
Isidro runs his fingers through the black mud, trying to figure out the reason for the failure.
But the mud holds no answers. All the clever ideas, the well-laid plans that he had put into it are nowhere to be found.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: We're out of time...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Why did I think I could replicate it in such a short time?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I should have known better... master said it took even the most skilled alchemists decades to create Corazonix...
The rusted Corazonix lies still in his pocket, as though mocking his incompetence.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: What happened?
She needed no answer. Broken parts litter the ground. The young man sits with his head hanging.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I'm sorry, Juana. I failed.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: It's alright, Isidro. This was my own choice.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: I'll face the consequences.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: It's too risky.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You heard the news. The kid failed. The compass is destroyed.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: All the more reason you shouldn't go.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: The Inquisition's demands were the compass and blueprints for a salt ship. How're you supposed to parley when we got neither?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Nobody said anything about delivering them personally.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: We just need to tell them where to pick them up themselves.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: You look like someone who can be reasoned with.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: If you mean the mate I sent to parley was too vulgar for you, no need to mince words.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: No, what I mean is that you must understand that trust is the basis for all cooperation.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I wouldn't have come myself if I wasn't trustworthy.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: And yet you've come empty-handed, asking me to go into the Salt Flat myself to retrieve the bargaining chips you're promising?

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: How am I to know you're not leading me into an ambush, with a hundred bandits armed to the teeth waiting for me?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Or maybe, I'm offering you more than just the compass and blueprints, but also the location of the pirate base and crewmen who already know how to sail a salt ship?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: No, Javier! This was supposed to give us a safe future, not make us their slaves!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Still better than following Juana to a watery death without the compass.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Besides, if you can understand, they can too. They'll cooperate when the Inquisition shows up.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: ...What about Juana?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: If I'm putting more chips on the table, then I need more in return.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Spare Juana.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: ...You will personally lead the way.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Negotiations are not over yet, Señor Alguacil.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Is that my concern?

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: ...What are you thinking?

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: He clearly isn't here in good faith. This so-called base of theirs is most certainly a trap.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Let me say this again: We have neither the manpower nor the resources for another major campaign.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: My men are in good shape. As for yours... I will ensure they are ready.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: I do not doubt your ability, but even if you do defeat the bandits, we cannot afford any more casualties.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: We will lack the manpower to build a ship, even if we acquire the blueprints. Aarón will remain trapped in the Salt Flat.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Your negotiations, your deals, none of this is my concern. I have gleaned the location of my enemies, and now I will act.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: The ships the bandits have used in their sin shall be put to the torch, along with their blueprints.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: As for the sinners... I will exterminate them.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Under whose authority?! The clerics you command grew up in Aarón. We've gone through countless hardships together.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Yet you fail to understand them... Nay, you have betrayed them.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: So why do you assume they will listen to you?
